pages.text: "Go away, you fool!" Nils the little bear shouted at the woods across the lake. The summer lakeshore was quiet, with only the reeds swaying. Shouting mean words again and again seemed fun.
"Go away, you fool—" The woods sent the words right back. Nils opened his eyes wide. "Oh? The woods answered me!" He wanted to shout louder and more often.
"Fool, fool, fool!" This time he shouted until his throat hurt. The woods repeated it three times too. "Fool, fool, fool—" Mean words came at Nils from everywhere. A shiver ran down his back.

Just then, Grandpa Bruno from the forest cabin came down through the trees. "Nils, what is all that shouting?" Nils spun around. "Go away too, Grandpa!" Without a word, Grandpa sat on a log by the water.
Alone, Nils shouted again. "Go away!" The woods answered, "Go away—" Nobody came. The lakeshore felt empty. Nils pouted. "...This is no fun at all."
Grandpa cupped both paws around his mouth and called across the lake. "Nils, come and play—" The woods sent it back. "Come and play—" The words reached Nils, making his heart feel warm and tickly.
"That is an echo. It gives back exactly the words you give it," Grandpa said. Nils tried a little call. "Hello—" The woods answered, "Hello—" His eyes sparkled. "Oh! Kind words come back kindly!"
Nils turned toward the log. "I am sorry I told you to go away." Grandpa opened his broad palm. Nils put his paw on it. Side by side, they called across the lake. "Thank you—!"

Nils shouted his rules across the lake. "One, hold back sharp words! Two, say sorry right away! Three, say thank you loudly!" The woods repeated every word. Nils raised both paws. "Kind words come back kindly!"
Grandpa bent his knees and wrapped both paws around Nils. Kind words return as kind words. "Grandpa, kind words come back kindly!"
